context.title: A Lamp unto My Feet
context.summary: In 176 verses the psalmist delights in God's word, seeks understanding, endures scorn and affliction, and asks God to revive and keep him by his promises.
context.background: No title. The longest psalm and longest chapter in the Bible. It is an alphabetic acrostic of 22 stanzas, one for each Hebrew letter; all eight verses in a stanza begin with that letter, which is why KJV prints ALEPH, BETH and so on. Nearly every verse names God's word with a synonym such as law, testimonies, precepts, statutes, commandments or judgments.

customs.note: A leather wineskin hung in a smoky tent turned dry, black and shriveled; the psalmist feels worn out.

watchFor: 'Thy word have I hid in mine heart' (v. 11) and 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet' (v. 105).
It ends not in triumph but 'I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant' (v. 176).

w: I will give thanks to you
and I will pay attention to
so let me pay attention to
and may they come to me
they have made an end of me
